title: Machine learning on quality-of-life scores defines subtypes tied to atezolizumab outcomes
summary: Consensus clustering of baseline quality-of-life scores in the IMpower150 trial identified two subtypes with median overall survival of 21.42 versus 13.14 months (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.64-2.62). A classifier assigned subtypes in the BIRCH, OAK and POPLAR cohorts, where ICI-versus-non-ICI hazard ratios were 1.30 (p=0.04) and 1.21 in the two subtypes in one validation analysis and 1.27 (p=0.007) and 1.21 (p=0.07) in OAK plus POPLAR. It is a post-hoc trial analysis with borderline effects; this is a version 1 preprint.
ai_technology: Consensus clustering of baseline quality-of-life scales with a classifier assigning subtypes to predict immunotherapy outcomes
organization: Zunyi Medical University; First People’s Hospital of Zunyi

evidence.tested: External validation cohorts from BIRCH, OAK and POPLAR randomized trials; post-hoc analysis.
evidence.unknown: Prospective validation, causal interpretation and robustness of the clustering; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Defines patient subtypes from questionnaire data that are associated with survival.
